Repository evidence

github.com/M-alasmary/
ACDS-Fullstack
01

The problem

Security operations, research experiments, and privileged administration require different permissions and safety boundaries. ACDS explores how one product can serve all three without flattening them into a single high-trust interface.

02

Engineering approach

The implementation uses a FastAPI and SQLAlchemy backend with a Next.js and TypeScript interface. Server-side roles drive three workspaces. Environment scopes separate production-style SOC resources from simulation-only research resources.

IDENTITY

Opaque sessions

HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookies; server-side token hashes; CSRF and origin checks on mutations.

AUTHORIZATION

Role + scope controls

Route permissions, ownership checks, environment scopes, and non-enumerable 404 responses.

OPERATIONS

Incident workflow

Acknowledge, investigate, escalate, low-risk response, approval-gated high-risk response, and emergency stop.

INTEGRITY

Audit chain

Hash-chained audit records with an endpoint that checks whether the chain has been altered.

03

Results & limitations

The repository documents 40 backend tests spanning authentication, MFA, CSRF, lockout, role matrices, scopes, IDOR controls, approvals, WebSockets, jobs, and audit integrity. It also names important limits: several navigation areas are guarded stubs, telemetry waits for collectors, rate limiting is per-process, and production migrations require Alembic.

No production-readiness, customer, detection-speed, or real-world performance claim is made here.
